structure: Part 4 read in full e2e/journeys.fit.spec.js (391 lines) and the shared helper e2e/support/journey.js (270 lines). journeys.fit.spec.js has two describe blocks. 'notification journeys end to end' runs one test per entry of JOURNEYS (5 tests: cattle by air, poultry by rail, pet cats by air, horse by sea, germinal bovine semen), each driven by walk() (notification type or category, origin, what are you importing, main import reason, commodity details, optional identification details, optional additional details, arrival details, optional transit countries, transporter, upload documents, roles and addresses with optional CPH and permanent address, contact address) then reviewAndSubmit() (hub shows every task Complete, review your notification, declaration with its empty-submit error, notification submitted, the submitted notification viewed by reference). 'the notification hub' has 4 tests: a fresh notification lists every task as to do, a hub task link returns to the hub after saving, review with tasks missing lists each incomplete section, and the submitted page is guarded until the declaration is confirmed. journey.js supplies the mount (/design-release-2.1), the page actions every step calls (field names, ids, button values) and the shared assertions (error summary title, back link, heading, reference format); only what these 9 tests drive or assert is claimed here. Claims are ordered: shared walk steps, the hub after completion, review, declaration, submitted page, view after submit, one claim per journey's distinguishing route and review content, then the four hub tests, then gaps.
